text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The business sections of all newspapers led with Securities Commission chairman Munir Majid urging Malaysia's futures exchanges to merge to avoid duplication and achieve economy of scales. But, he said the regulator will not force the merger between Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the Malaysia Monetary Exchange and the Kuala Lumpur Commodities Exchange.

-- Telekom Malaysia has signed two agreements with Marconi SpA and GEC-Marconi Ltd in London to set up joint research units in Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor, a high technology zone just outside Kuala Lumpur. Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, starting a two-month work-and-holiday break from Monday, was present at the signing.
-- A business expectations survey covering 220 public limit companies showed that they expect their gross revenue to increase by 5.6 percent to a total 102.01 billion ringgit.
-- Esso Malaysia Bhd said it expects natural gas output to rise by 10 percent this year, but crude production would remain stable.
